text:
marta: Heads-up — nightly eval on main shows a sudden quality spike for the summarization prompts, failure rate from 4% -> 18% after last runtime push. cc @alex @jyoti

alex: saw that too. suspiciously correlated with the prefetch/batching change we rolled yesterday (small-queue-prefetch).

jyoti: can you paste the failing example IDs? I want to see if they share prefixes.

marta: sure, snippet from eval runner: `fail_ids = ["s-8721","s-8724","s-8729","s-8731"]`. Many of them start with the same first 12 tokens in the prompt set.

chen: interesting — that matches the prefix-cache key window. We recently shrank the shorthash from 64->48 bits to save memory; might increase collisions under heavy prefetch.

jyoti: do we have collision counts over the run?

marta: paste from nightly logs: ```
[2026-03-18T03:02:12Z] prefix_cache: lookups=1_200_320 hits=1_196_012 collisions=4_308 eviction_skips=120
[2026-03-18T03:02:12Z] batching: avg_batch=6.2 prefetch_inflight=42
```

alex: collisions=4k seems high. Before the change it was ~90 for a similar workload.

jyoti: hypothesis: collision -> wrong KV prefix served -> generation drifts -> eval fails. We should confirm determinism by replaying exact requests with and without prefix cache.

marta: I ran a small repro: two identical requests sent concurrently, one got different continuation. Attached diff of outputs: `outA != outB` (same seed).

chen: can you capture the exact cache key hash for the two requests? `cache_key = shorthash(prefix_tokens)` logging might show collision.

marta: added logging and repro run: `keys = [0x7fa2b1, 0x9fa2b1, 0x7fa2b1]` — you can see duplicate `0x7fa2b1` for two different prefixes.

jyoti: confirmation. That explains nondeterminism. Two different prefixes collapsed to same slot. Then later KV reads pull wrong context.

alex: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback shorthash to 64 bits (memory cost), 2) add tenant+seq salt to key (reduces collisions), 3) disable prefetch under high inflight. Which is fastest?

chen: fastest is to disable prefetch in the runtime flags for the affected pool (no restart across nodes) — toggle weight to 0. That should reduce collision surface since fewer concurrent prefetches will compete for slots.

marta: can we toggle for canary first? deploy-bot, can we flip `runtime.prefetch.enabled=false` for canary pool `eng-ml-canary`?

deploy-bot: Received request to set `runtime.prefetch.enabled=false` for pool `eng-ml-canary`. Scheduling change across 3 nodes. ETA 60s. :gear:

sre-bot: Note: changing prefetch will lower throughput. Watch queue depth and latency SLOs. Alerting paused for 10m to avoid noise.

(1m later) deploy-bot: Change applied on all 3 nodes in pool `eng-ml-canary`.

marta: re-ran the nightly subset against canary — failures dropped to 5.1%. Significant improvement.

alex: good signal. Still need permanent fix: revert shorthash change + add a long-term eviction policy that uses LRU+prefix fingerprint.

jyoti: I'll open a PR: `runtime: increase shorthash to 64b; add tenant salt to key` and include a toggle to enable new keying. Also add unit test that simulates collision and checks KV lookup correctness.

chen: also file an incident ticket for tracking: INC-2026-042, link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-042

marta: noted. For immediate rollout path we should: 1) keep prefetch off on canary, 2) roll shorthash revert to staging with heavy stress, 3) run nightly evals.

jyoti: I'll schedule the revert PR for staging today and tag @chen for rollout.

alex: quick reminder — add a regression test in nightly-evals that uses near-colliding prefixes to catch future shorthash reductions.

marta: added to checklist. Thanks team — great catch. :tada:

chen: #followup — measure memory delta if we revert to 64b so product knows cost impact.

marta: will include memory/latency matrix in the incident ticket.

(near end) deploy-bot: Canary metrics: latency +8% p95 under stress test after prefetch toggle. Queue depth +2. Continue to monitor.

alex: OK closing the triage here; keep updates in INC-2026-042, leaving prefetch disabled on canary until after revert tests.
